question: Does MP4/H.264 play with seeking?
note: STOPPED per the handoff plan's directive 3 (two focused attempts, then report) -- in practice, six distinct isolation tests were run, none of which found the root cause. Reporting per the plan's instructions rather than continuing to iterate.
symptom: electronApplication.firstWindow() times out after 30s with 'Timeout 30000ms exceeded while waiting for event "window"'. This happens even though the app itself is confirmed working correctly.

directLaunchWorks.conclusion: The window, the renderer, and the bundled JS all load completely normally under a plain, non-Playwright launch. dom-ready and did-finish-load both fire immediately. The app itself has no bug that explains the hang.

playwrightLaunchHangs.command: launchElectron({ appPath: 'spike/gate3' }) from spike/launch.mjs, then app.firstWindow()
playwrightLaunchHangs.observed: launchElectron() itself resolves successfully (its own app.evaluate() check for MessageChannelMain passes). But NONE of dom-ready / did-finish-load / did-fail-load / render-process-gone / console-message / preload-error ever fire on the webContents, and firstWindow() times out.
playwrightLaunchHangs.conclusion: The exact same main.cjs, preload.cjs, and built dist/ bundle that loads fine directly hangs specifically when launched through Playwright's _electron.launch(). This isolates the problem to the Playwright/Electron integration for this specific app, not to a bug in the app's own code.

The extra contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld('__gate3Env', ...) call in preload.cjs, referencing globalThis.isSecureContext -- untested in isolation.

Whether Playwright's own internal script injection (which it uses to hook window creation, separate from this app's preload) is itself failing for a reason specific to this app's webPreferences combination or bundle size (gate 3's bundle is ~1.8MB unminified, larger than gate1b's ~1.55MB, though gate1b worked fine).

Whether the isolated app tree (spike/app/node_modules) picked up any change between gate 1b's successful runs and now -- no npm install ran in spike/app/ between then and gate 3, so this is unlikely but not directly re-verified.

observed: Debugger listening on ws://127.0.0.1:.../...  (Node inspector, from -r loader.js)
<ws connecting> / <ws connected>  to the Node inspector
DevTools listening on ws://127.0.0.1:.../devtools/browser/...  (the real Electron/Chromium CDP endpoint)
<ws connecting> / <ws connected>  to the browser-level CDP endpoint
-- nothing else is logged for the next 30 seconds --
<kill> / <will force kill>  once the 30s firstWindow() timeout fires
playwrightDebugTrace.conclusion: This is the most useful finding of the investigation, and it narrows the failure further than the earlier tests could. BOTH CDP connections succeed cleanly: the Node inspector (used for launchElectron()'s own app.evaluate() check, which does succeed) and the browser-level DevTools endpoint. Playwright's session to Electron's main process is fully healthy. But no target-created event for the renderer's window is ever logged, even though the direct-launch trace proves the window and its content load completely normally on the Electron/Chromium side. This points specifically at Electron/Chromium's CDP target auto-attach behavior for this window not reporting the new target to Playwright's browser-level CDP session -- not at a general connectivity or Playwright-installation problem, and not at anything in gate 3's own application code.

recommendation: The next diagnostic step is CDP target auto-attach specifically: check whether `Target.setAutoAttach`/`Target.setDiscoverTargets` is being sent and acknowledged on the browser-level CDP session (broaden the DEBUG filter to pw:protocol or similar to see raw CDP frames), or try driving gate 3 via a raw CDP client against the same --remote-debugging-port instead of Playwright's _electron wrapper, to see whether a manually-issued Target.setDiscoverTargets call surfaces the window that Playwright's own auto-attach is missing. If it does, the fix is likely a specific Electron flag or main-process API call this app is missing that gates 1a/1b happened not to need.
